q: Lenses produce images similar to images formed by curved mirrors, but they do so by _____ light rather than reflecting it.
e: Lenses produce images by refracting light rather than reflecting it.

q: For refraction at spherical surface, the radius $R$ is _____ if the surface is convex toward the object.
e: The radius R is positive if the surface is convex toward the object.

q: For refraction at spherical surface, the radius $R$ is negative if the surface is _____ toward the object.
e: The radius R is negative if the surface is concave toward the object.

q: If the rays are paraxial, then the angles $\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \theta_1$ and $\theta_2$ are very _____.
e: If the rays are paraxial, the angles are very small.

q: In the equation for refraction at a single spherical surface, if the first medium is air, $n_1$ is equal to _____.
e: If the first medium is air, its refractive index n1 is 1.

q: We define focal length, $f$ of a lens as the image distance when the object is at _____.
e: Focal length is defined as the image distance when the object is at infinity.

q: The object distance $u$ and the image distance $v$ are measured from the _____ of the lens $P$.
e: Object and image distances are measured from the centre of the lens P.

q: According to the sign convention for lenses, distances of real object, real image and real focus are _____.
e: Distances of real object, real image and real focus are positive.

q: According to the sign convention for lenses, distances of virtual object, virtual image and virtual focus are _____.
e: Distances of virtual object, virtual image and virtual focus are negative.

q: According to the sign convention for lenses, the perpendicular distance measured _____ the principal axis is positive.
e: Perpendicular distance measured above the principal axis is positive.

q: According to the sign convention for lenses, the perpendicular distance measured below the principal axis is _____.
e: Perpendicular distance measured below the principal axis is negative.

q: The lens-makers' equation relates the focal length to the refractive index and the radii of _____.
e: The lens-makers' equation uses the radii of curvature of the lens surfaces.

q: A transparent material which can diverge or converge rays of light is called a _____.
e: A transparent material which can diverge or converge rays of light is called a lens.

q: A lens has at least one _____ surface.
e: A lens has at least one curved surface.

q: Generally, lenses are made up of glass with two _____ surfaces.
e: Generally, lenses are made up of glass with two spherical surfaces.

q: There are two main types of lenses, known as convex (or converging) lens and _____ (or diverging) lens.
e: The two main types of lenses are convex and concave lenses.

q: The convex lens is used as a magnifying _____.
e: The convex lens is used as a magnifying glass.

q: The lenses in spectacles used by a short-sighted person are _____ lenses.
e: Spectacles for short-sighted persons use concave lenses.

q: The lenses in spectacles used by a long-sighted person are _____ lenses.
e: Spectacles for long-sighted persons use convex lenses.

q: A convex lens is thicker in the _____ than at the edges.
e: A convex lens is thicker in the middle than at the edges.

q: Three types of convex lens are bi-convex, plano-convex and converging _____.
e: The three types of convex lens are bi-convex, plano-convex and converging meniscus.

q: A concave lens is thinner in the _____ than at the edges.
e: A concave lens is thinner in the middle than at the edges.

q: Three types of concave lens are bi-concave, plano-concave and diverging _____.
e: The three types of concave lens are bi-concave, plano-concave and diverging meniscus.

q: The line joining the centres of curvature of two surfaces is the _____ axis of a lens.
e: The principal axis is the line joining the centres of curvature of two surfaces.

q: If the radii of curvature of the two surfaces of a lens are equal, the lens is said to be _____.
e: A lens with equal radii of curvature is said to be symmetric.

q: A point in the middle of a symmetric lens on the principle axis is the _____ centre of a lens.
e: The optical centre is a point in the middle of a symmetric lens on the principle axis.

q: The rays parallel to the principal axis converge at a point on the principal axis after refraction through a convex lens; this point is called the principal _____.
e: The point where parallel rays converge is called the principal focus.

q: Since the rays actually pass through the focus, the focus of the convex lens is _____.
e: The focus of a convex lens is real because rays actually pass through it.

q: The distance between centre of a convex lens and its focus is called focal _____ of the convex lens.
e: The distance between the centre and focus is the focal length.

q: The rays parallel to the principal axis are _____ after refraction through a concave lens.
e: Parallel rays become divergent after refraction through a concave lens.

q: Since the divergent rays do not actually pass through the principal focus, the focus of the concave lens is _____.
e: The focus of a concave lens is virtual.

q: A lens has _____ foci.
e: A lens has two focal points or foci.

q: The points at a distance of twice the focal length from the centre of lens are represented by _____.
e: Points at twice the focal length are represented by 2F.

q: A ray parallel to the principal axis passes through the _____ after refraction through a convex lens.
e: A ray parallel to the principal axis passes through the focus.

q: A ray passing through the focus of a convex lens emerges _____ to the principal axis.
e: A ray passing through the focus emerges parallel to the principal axis.

q: A ray passing through the _____ of lens emerges in the same direction.
e: A ray passing through the centre of the lens emerges in the same direction.

q: When the object is at infinity, its image formed by a convex lens is at _____.
e: When the object is at infinity, the image is formed at F.

q: When the object is at infinity, the image formed by a convex lens is real, inverted, and _____ than the object.
e: The image is smaller than the object when the object is at infinity.

q: Due to the property of forming an image at $F$ for an object at infinity, a convex lens can be used as object lens of a _____.
e: Convex lenses are used as the object lens of a telescope.

q: When the object is beyond $2F$, the image formed by a convex lens is between $F$ and _____.
e: The image is formed between F and 2F when the object is beyond 2F.

q: When the object is beyond $2F$, the image formed by a convex lens is real, inverted, and _____ than the object.
e: The image is smaller than the object when the object is beyond 2F.

q: Due to the property of forming a smaller real image for an object beyond $2F$, a convex lens can be used in a _____.
e: Convex lenses are used in a camera.

q: When the object is at $2F$, the image formed by a convex lens is real, inverted, and of the _____ size as the object.
e: The image is of the same size as the object when the object is at 2F.

q: Due to the property of forming an equal-sized real image for an object at $2F$, a convex lens can be used in a _____ making equal-sized copy.
e: Convex lenses are used in a photocopier.

q: When the object is between $F$ and $2F$, the image formed by a convex lens is beyond _____.
e: The image is formed beyond 2F when the object is between F and 2F.

q: When the object is between $F$ and $2F$, the image formed by a convex lens is real, inverted, and _____ than the object.
e: The image is larger than the object when the object is between F and 2F.

q: Due to the property of forming a larger real image for an object between $F$ and $2F$, a convex lens can be used in a _____.
e: Convex lenses are used in a projector.

q: When the object is at $F$, the image formed by a convex lens is at _____.
e: The image is formed at infinity when the object is at F.

q: Due to the property of forming an image at infinity for an object at $F$, a convex lens can be used in a _____ to produce parallel beam.
e: Convex lenses are used in a spotlight.

q: When the object is between $F$ and $P$, the image formed by a convex lens is behind the object, virtual, erect, and _____ than the object.
e: The image is larger than the object when the object is between F and P.

q: Due to the property of forming a larger virtual erect image for an object between $F$ and $P$, a convex lens can be used as a magnifying _____.
e: Convex lenses are used as a magnifying glass.

q: The image formed by a concave lens is always virtual, erect and _____ than the object.
e: The image formed by a concave lens is always smaller than the object.

q: The image formed by a concave lens is formed between $P$ and $F$ on the _____ side of the lens as the object.
e: The image is formed on the same side of the lens as the object.

q: A convex lens can produce both real and _____ images depending on the position of the object.
e: A convex lens can produce both real and virtual images.

q: A concave lens can produce only _____ image.
e: A concave lens can produce only virtual images.

q: The virtual image formed by the convex or concave lens is the same size as the object only when the object is in _____ with the lens.
e: The virtual image is the same size only when the object is in contact with the lens.

q: The magnification is the ratio of the height of the image to the height of the _____.
e: Magnification is the ratio of image height to object height.

q: The magnification can be expressed as the ratio of image distance to _____ distance.
e: Magnification is the ratio of image distance to object distance.

q: Curved mirrors form images by reflecting light, whereas lenses produce images by _____ light.
e: Lenses produce images by refracting light.

q: If a spherical surface is convex toward the object, its radius of curvature $R$ is considered _____.
e: The radius of curvature R is positive if convex toward the object.

q: If a spherical surface is concave toward the object, its radius of curvature $R$ is considered _____.
e: The radius of curvature R is negative if concave toward the object.

q: Distances of real focus are _____ according to the sign convention for lenses.
e: Distances of real focus are positive.

q: Distances of virtual focus are _____ according to the sign convention for lenses.
e: Distances of virtual focus are negative.

q: A transparent material which can _____ or converge rays of light is called a lens.
e: A lens can diverge or converge rays of light.

q: A transparent material which can diverge or _____ rays of light is called a lens.
e: A lens can diverge or converge rays of light.

q: A converging lens is also known as a _____ lens.
e: A converging lens is a convex lens.

q: A diverging lens is also known as a _____ lens.
e: A diverging lens is a concave lens.

q: A lens which is thicker in the middle than at the edges is a _____ lens.
e: A convex lens is thicker in the middle.

q: A lens which is thinner in the middle than at the edges is a _____ lens.
e: A concave lens is thinner in the middle.

q: The focus of a convex lens is real because the rays actually _____ through it.
e: Rays actually pass through the focus of a convex lens.

q: The focus of a concave lens is virtual because the divergent rays do not actually _____ through that point.
e: Divergent rays do not actually pass through the virtual focus.

q: When an object is at infinity, the image formed by a convex lens is inverted and _____ than the object.
e: The image is smaller than the object.

q: When an object is at $2F$, the image formed by a convex lens is real and of the _____ size as the object.
e: The image is of the same size as the object.

q: When an object is between $F$ and $P$, the image formed by a convex lens is virtual, erect, and _____ than the object.
e: The image is larger than the object.

q: The image formed by a concave lens is always virtual, _____ and smaller than the object.
e: The image is always erect.

q: The image formed by a concave lens is always _____, erect and smaller than the object.
e: The image is always virtual.

q: The principal axis of a lens is the line joining the _____ of curvature of two surfaces.
e: The principal axis joins the centres of curvature.

q: The optical centre of a lens is a point in the middle of a _____ lens on the principle axis.
e: The optical centre is in the middle of a symmetric lens.

q: The points at a distance of _____ the focal length from the centre of lens are represented by $2F$.
e: 2F represents points at twice the focal length.

q: When the object is between $F$ and $2F$, the image formed by a convex lens is real, inverted, and formed beyond _____.
e: The image is formed beyond 2F.

q: When the object is beyond $2F$, the image formed by a convex lens is real, inverted, and formed between $F$ and _____.
e: The image is formed between F and 2F.

q: The image formed by a concave lens is formed between $P$ and _____ on the same side of the lens as the object.
e: The image is formed between P and F.

q: When the object is at the principal focus $F$, the image formed by a convex lens is at _____.
e: The image is formed at infinity.

q: A concave lens can produce only _____ images.
e: A concave lens produces only virtual images.

q: The virtual image formed by a lens is the same size as the object only when the object is in _____ with the lens.
e: The image is the same size when the object is in contact with the lens.

q: A principal ray passing through the _____ of a lens emerges in the same direction without deviation.
e: A ray passing through the centre emerges in the same direction.

q: Bi-convex and bi-concave lens are widely used; for simplicity, a bi-convex lens will be called a _____ lens.
e: A bi-convex lens is simply called a convex lens.

q: The power of a lens is inversely proportional to the _____ of the lens.
e: Power is inversely proportional to focal length.

q: The shorter the focal length the _____ is the power of the lens.
e: A shorter focal length means greater power.

q: Since the focal length of a convex lens is positive in sign it has a _____ power.
e: A convex lens has positive power.

q: The focal length of a concave lens is negative so that it has a _____ power.
e: A concave lens has negative power.

q: If a lens has a focal length of 1 metre, it has one unit power or one _____.
e: One unit of power is one dioptre.

q: The unit of power of a lens is denoted by the letter _____.
e: The unit dioptre is denoted by D.

q: If the focal length $f$ is measured in metre, the power $P$ is equal to _____.
e: P = 1/f when f is in metres.

q: If the focal length $f$ is measured in centimetre, the power $P$ is equal to _____.
e: P = 100/f when f is in centimetres.

q: The power of a lens is _____ proportional to the focal length of the lens.
e: Power is inversely proportional to focal length.

q: A lens with a shorter focal length has a _____ power.
e: A shorter focal length gives greater power.

q: A lens with a positive focal length has a _____ power.
e: Positive focal length means positive power.

q: A lens with a negative focal length has a _____ power.
e: Negative focal length means negative power.

q: One dioptre is the power of a lens with a focal length of _____ metre.
e: One dioptre corresponds to a focal length of 1 metre.
